newsitem.title: UK: UK building societies welcome new law.
newsitem.headline: UK building societies welcome new law.

text.p: The Building Societies Association (BSA), which represents UK mutually-owned savings and loan institutions, on Thursday welcomed the passing of the new Building Societies Act.

It said the legislation would allow the societies to compete on a level footing with all other financial institutions in the UK, changing the "prescriptive" regime of previous legislation to a "permissive" one.

The new law, which had been in danger of not being passed because of Britain's impending election, has been criticised by some building societies who are planning to convert to bank status and float on the stock exchange in the next few months.
The law includes clauses which remove a converting society's five-year immunity from takeover if the new bank buys another financial institution or if 75 percent of shareholders vote to abandon it.
The BSA said the new Act would also introduce enhanced accountability of society boards to their members.
"I am delighted that the bill has been passed by Parliament," said BSA director-general Adrian Coles. "It is an important piece of legislation for societies and their customers."
Coles particularly welcomed the clauses taking away the five-year immunity without which, he said, converting societies would have had an unfair advantage over other financial institutions.
"This was unacceptable in the increasingly competitive financial services marketplace," Coles added.
